sources.title: AI Companies Are Buying Antique Books, Ingesting Their Contents to Train Models, and Then Destroying Them at Incredible Scale, Even If Almost No Copies Remain - Futurism
passages: But many companies, including Anthropic, have turned to ingesting physical books instead, which they can buy countless used copies of on the cheap.

According to the settled lawsuit , Anthropic used a hydraulic powered cutting machine to neatly remove the pages from the books it procured from book resellers and then scanned them using industrial-grade imaging equipment.
In other words, it was literally ripping off authors’ books to train its AI.

One small book seller said that in April, he suddenly went from selling no more than 20 books a week to hundreds, and he’s almost certain that the customers are AI labs, noting the random selection of the books and how they all have ISBNs.
He added that his inventory is full with rare and out of print books, meaning that an AI company could be destroying some of the few remaining copies that can be found.

And since Anthropic was turning the original physical texts into digital ones — rather than redistributing them as new copies — a judge found this to be “transformative,” and therefore protected by fair use.
“The optics problem is real,” ISBNdb’s site says. “‘AI company destroys two million books’ is not a headline that generates sympathy.”
I’m a tech and science correspondent for Futurism, where I’m particularly interested in astrophysics, the business and ethics of artificial intelligence and automation, and the environment.

extraction.body: Can’t-miss innovations from the bleeding edge of science and tech Traditionally, books have been good for two things: reading, and looking nice on a shelf. To those building large language models, books are nothing more than fodder to be devoured en masse before being spit out like fishbone. Often, they’re happy to use digital books — or even better, pirated digital books, as Meta has been accused of doing, and as Anthropic was forced to pay a $1.5 billion settlement to authors for also doing. But many companies, including Anthropic, have turned to ingesting physical books instead, which they can buy countless used copies of on the cheap. According to the settled lawsuit , Anthropic used a hydraulic powered cutting machine to neatly remove the pages from the books it procured from book resellers and then scanned them using industrial-grade imaging equipment. In other words, it was literally ripping off authors’ books to train its AI. This process took advantage of a legal concept known as first-sale doctrine, which allows a buyer to do what they want with a purchase without the original copyright holder’s say-so. And since Anthropic was turning the original physical texts into digital ones — rather than redistributing them as new copies — a judge found this to be “transformative,” and therefore protected by fair use. Now, as 404 Media reports , this practice has become prevalent enough that even well-established book sellers are looking to cash in on the AI boom. One called ISBNdb, which boasts the “world’s largest book database,” extolls that the “world’s best AI training data is setting on a shelf,” upholding these physical texts as uncorrupted by shoddy AI writing that’s already polluted so much of the internet (and indeed, newer books ). “Print books from the pre-LLM era are structurally guaranteed to be free of this contamination. That alone is a significant advantage,” it explains in an article on its website, as quoted by 404 . “Physical books published before this date [pre-2022] are structurally clean of modern poisoning tools.” Once focused on helping libraries, distributors, and book shops find and sell books, ISBNdb now helps AI companies bulk-buy anywhere between 1,000 to one million books per order, according to 404 . As an added bonus, it also promises AI companies that it’ll keep their purchases under wraps — nobody wants to end up in the spotlight like Anthropic and Meta, obviously — while clearly sounding aware about how incredibly shady the practice sounds. “The optics problem is real,” ISBNdb’s site says. “‘AI company destroys two million books’ is not a headline that generates sympathy.” One small book seller said that in April, he suddenly went from selling no more than 20 books a week to hundreds, and he’s almost certain that the customers are AI labs, noting the random selection of the books and how they all have ISBNs. He added that his inventory is full with rare and out of print books, meaning that an AI company could be destroying some of the few remaining copies that can be found. “I personally have mixed feelings about all of this,” the bookseller told 404 . “It benefits me financially as well as by clearing out old inventory that is otherwise unlikely to sell. I’ve been well-suited for these sales with inventory from overseas and foreign language books. On the other hand, I don’t like the end-use, and I don’t like that uncommon books are being pulped.” More antique books may be endangered. 404 noted how rare booksellers in the Netherlands are being inundated with bulk purchases they believe are being made by AI companies , though they can’t know for sure. Similar suspicions are being felt all throughout the industry. Services like ISBNdb facilitate these bulk orders, keeping the AI buyers anonymous as promised. There may be strong hints thats a bulk order is for an AI lab, but booksellers can, for the most part, merely speculate. extraction.body: When a startup shuts down or gets acquired, its most valuable asset may no longer be its code, patents, or customer lists—but rather the communication records its employees used every day. As artificial intelligence (AI) evolves from chatbots into autonomous digital workers, AI data companies are aggressively acquiring internal datasets from defunct companies, including Slack chat logs, Google Drive files, emails, and Zoom meeting recordings, with individual offers reaching as high as $300,000 (approximately NT$9.6 million). AI data company Mercor has been actively targeting failed or acquired startups, seeking to purchase their internal datasets. Mercor is the data supplier behind AI giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic, and its reach has now extended from publicly available internet content into the most private communication trails within enterprises. In late June, AI agent startup Warmly announced it would be acquired by HubSpot. Just eight days later, Warmly founder and CEO Max Greenwald received an email from Mercor seeking to purchase or license Warmly's internal data—including Slack chat logs, GitHub records, Asana project management content, Google Drive files, and employee meeting transcripts—with offers reaching up to $300,000. In the days that followed, Warmly received multiple similar inquiries from Mercor and other AI data companies, but Greenwald ultimately turned them all down. AI data companies buying books and startup code is hardly news, but as AI giants accelerate development of autonomous AI agents, the nature of data demand is undergoing a fundamental shift. Public internet content, books, and code are no longer sufficient to support the training needs of next-generation AI models. Bobby Samuels, CEO of data company Protege, put it bluntly: AI labs have essentially "scraped the entire internet," and what they need now is real human-to-human interaction. Protege primarily helps companies assess whether their internal data qualifies for sale or licensing. This year alone, the company has processed at least $100 million (approximately NT$3 billion) in data transactions—a more than threefold increase from roughly $30 million (approximately NT$1 billion) in the same period last year. The following table shows the change in data transaction volume handled by Protege: Note: Figures disclosed by Protege CEO Bobby Samuels. When AI transitions from a chatbot that simply answers questions to a digital worker that can genuinely share the workload, it needs far more than just "what the answer is"—it needs to understand "how humans actually get work done." For example: how a human employee responds when a customer raises an issue; how an engineer troubleshoots step by step when an IT system fails; how a finance staffer handles an invoice discrepancy; how a salesperson updates customer records in a CRM system. Even the specific clicks and inputs an employee makes when software suddenly throws an error. These real-world work experiences are nearly impossible to find on the public internet. An IT ticket might record "employee unable to log into website," followed by Slack chat logs showing engineers discussing the root cause, emails containing the final resolution, and a GitHub commit documenting a related code fix. To a human, this is just routine troubleshooting. But to an AI agent, it is an entire set of highly valuable "on-the-job training"—precisely the material needed to train AI systems capable of autonomous task execution. This emerging business is far more complicated than it appears on the surface. Companies involved must navigate thorny issues around privacy and intellectual property. Slack conversations may contain customer information, emails may include employee names, meeting transcripts may reveal trade secrets, and data from healthcare companies may even involve patient privacy. All such data must undergo anonymization before it can be legally sold or licensed to AI companies. Warmly CEO Greenwald's decision to decline selling internal data reflects the reservations some entrepreneurs hold about such transactions. Even when a company is about to be acquired or has already shut down, internal communication records may still implicate the privacy of employees, customers, and partners. Yet the rapid expansion of the data trading market signals that the AI industry's demand for "real work data" is forming an irreversible wave. Protege's data transaction volume surging from $30 million to $100 million in a single year is the most direct quantitative proof of this trend. As the AI agent race heats up, the digital legacies of failed companies—those traces of human work scattered across Slack, email, and meeting recordings—are becoming the scarcest raw material for AI training. And how to strike a balance between data demand and privacy protection will be the core challenge this emerging industry must confront going forward. story.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models

facts.text: Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that construct simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models.
And Bloomberg reported in September that SpaceX’s AI unit is weighing buying data from struggling startups.
Demand for defunct companies’ data emerged suddenly last year, as AI training labs hit the limits of public and synthetic datasets.
In total, Google is picking up 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams chats, 30 million lines of code – but not records of loyalty program members or other customer data.
Spirit Airlines collapsed in May this year, but its data is set for a new lease of life after Google acquired it in an auction.

Alongside the data, Google's $10 million also buys it all of Spirit's internally developed software and applications, including all the source code , plugins, data files, libraries, APIs and documentation.
The tech giant recently outbid AI company Mercor to acquire the de-identified data, according to court documents .
Google bid $10 million, versus Mercor's $7.5 million, though reports note the bidding started around the $5 million mark.
"We acquired part of an enterprise dataset from Spirit Airlines, which can be helpful in improving our products and AI models,” the spokesperson said.
AI developers are struggling to find enough data to train their models, sparking a bidding war for failed Spirit Airlines deidentified data

The data bought by Google includes all productivity and collaboration data, which the filing notes includes everything from emails to chats, spreadsheets to calendars, as well as "core business systems and business applications data".
Anthropic has raised eyebrows via a campaign of buying up pre-2022 books to scan for training data, while Google was reportedly trying to buy code from Google Play Store app developers.
SimpleClosure helps failed startups sell their old code, chats, and emails to AI companies, and Meta had to pause plans to track its own employees for AI training purposes amid internal backlash.
"We will not receive any personal information from this dataset," the Google spokesperson added.
"Any data we receive will be rigorously scrubbed of any personally identifiable information by a third party before receipt."

This includes data on employee behavior and productivity, aircraft operations, and inventory, among other topics.

extraction.body: BANGKOK/WASHINGTON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - The International Monetary Fund warned on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing risks from an artificial intelligence-driven selloff, rising government bond yields, or cyberattacks as potential threats facing still-resilient markets. The IMF said in its ‌Global Financial Stability Report that AI investments have so far helped offset economic drags from war in the Middle East and overall policy ‌uncertainty. But it noted "growing evidence" that AI capabilities may not require as much investment, or the potential economic gains may not be as large as expected. "An AI market correction will affect ​the real economy," Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director in the IMF's Monetary and Capital Markets Department, said at a press briefing in Bangkok. He said while global risk sentiment was very strong, underpinned by solid earnings and optimism about AI, such "resilience is not necessarily safety". An AI correction would have impacts on wealth and investment that could spill into broader markets, he said. The risk of such a selloff, as well as a spike in sovereign bond yields or a major cyberattack, were among "plausible near-term ‌catalysts" that policymakers should monitor, the IMF said ⁠in its report. While each of these risks might be manageable on its own, they also could trigger vulnerabilities with potential systemic implications, Vamvakidis said. Should the momentum in AI investment slow, the IMF noted growing leverage in the sector could exacerbate any shock ⁠by triggering forced selling and higher volatility. For example, hyperscalers now represent 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance, up from less than 1% in 2024. "The consequences of an AI correction could be global," the IMF warned, as it called on policymakers to curb leverage use, including derivatives and margin loans, where it is "excessive." The IMF said ​bond ​market risks have worsened since its April report, as higher energy prices have driven ​government bond yields up. Historically high sovereign debt levels and ‌unresolved fiscal deficits in major economies were adding to the pressure. "The market is concerned about absorption potential of the huge issuance that is coming from the sovereigns and increasingly also from the private sector, at the time that central banks are shrinking their balances, and we have to rely more on price-sensitive investors," Vamvakidis said. The IMF report said bond markets have so far dealt with the stress well, with hedge funds able to unwind some of their repurchase agreement borrowing without triggering turmoil in repo markets. The group called on policymakers to put public debt on a sustainable path. On cyber threats, the ‌IMF said that a lack of resources, particularly in emerging markets, and a growing reliance ​on a small number of critical providers was making cyber defense more difficult. In over 70% of ​cases so far in 2026, software providers have had almost no ​time to patch vulnerabilities before they were exploited, a 20 percentage point jump from a year ago, the IMF said. ‌It noted that while AI can help address some of these risks, ​models were also making cyberattacks more ​sophisticated. The IMF cautioned that a major attack affecting a critical service or financial institution could undermine confidence, which could quickly ripple throughout markets. It called on policymakers to boost cybersecurity capacity, including stricter oversight of third-party technology vendors. The IMF said its stress test models showed banks' ​capital cushions remained robust even in a hypothetical downturn ‌triggered by an AI slowdown and bond market fragility. But it warned of "pockets of weakness," with banks representing 22% of global ​banking assets found to have "weak" capital levels under the test, up from 18% under the 2025 test. (Reporting by Pete Schroeder in ​Washington and Selena Li in Bangkok; Editing by Andrea Ricci and John Mair)

extraction.body: BANGKOK/WASHINGTON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - The International Monetary Fund warned on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing risks from an artificial intelligence-driven selloff, rising government bond yields, or cyberattacks as potential threats facing still-resilient markets. The IMF said in its ‌Global Financial Stability Report that AI investments have so far helped offset economic drags from war in the Middle East and overall policy ‌uncertainty. But it noted "growing evidence" that AI capabilities may not require as much investment, or the potential economic gains may not be as large as expected. "An AI market correction will affect ​the real economy," Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director in the IMF's Monetary and Capital Markets Department, said at a press briefing in Bangkok. He said while global risk sentiment was very strong, underpinned by solid earnings and optimism about AI, such "resilience is not necessarily safety". An AI correction would have impacts on wealth and investment that could spill into broader markets, he said. The risk of such a selloff, as well as a spike in sovereign bond yields or a major cyberattack, were among "plausible near-term ‌catalysts" that policymakers should monitor, the IMF said ⁠in its report. While each of these risks might be manageable on its own, they also could trigger vulnerabilities with potential systemic implications, Vamvakidis said. Should the momentum in AI investment slow, the IMF noted growing leverage in the sector could exacerbate any shock ⁠by triggering forced selling and higher volatility. For example, hyperscalers now represent 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance, up from less than 1% in 2024. "The consequences of an AI correction could be global," the IMF warned, as it called on policymakers to curb leverage use, including derivatives and margin loans, where it is "excessive." The IMF said ​bond ​market risks have worsened since its April report, as higher energy prices have driven ​government bond yields up. Historically high sovereign debt levels and ‌unresolved fiscal deficits in major economies were adding to the pressure. "The market is concerned about absorption potential of the huge issuance that is coming from the sovereigns and increasingly also from the private sector, at the time that central banks are shrinking their balances, and we have to rely more on price-sensitive investors," Vamvakidis said. The IMF report said bond markets have so far dealt with the stress well, with hedge funds able to unwind some of their repurchase agreement borrowing without triggering turmoil in repo markets. The group called on policymakers to put public debt on a sustainable path. On cyber threats, the ‌IMF said that a lack of resources, particularly in emerging markets, and a growing reliance ​on a small number of critical providers was making cyber defense more difficult. In over 70% of ​cases so far in 2026, software providers have had almost no ​time to patch vulnerabilities before they were exploited, a 20 percentage point jump from a year ago, the IMF said. ‌It noted that while AI can help address some of these risks, ​models were also making cyberattacks more ​sophisticated. The IMF cautioned that a major attack affecting a critical service or financial institution could undermine confidence, which could quickly ripple throughout markets. It called on policymakers to boost cybersecurity capacity, including stricter oversight of third-party technology vendors. The IMF said its stress test models showed banks' ​capital cushions remained robust even in a hypothetical downturn ‌triggered by an AI slowdown and bond market fragility. But it warned of "pockets of weakness," with banks representing 22% of global ​banking assets found to have "weak" capital levels under the test, up from 18% under the 2025 test. (Reporting by Pete Schroeder in ​Washington and Selena Li in Bangkok; Editing by Andrea Ricci and John Mair)

However, it noted "growing evidence" that AI capabilities might not require as much investment as previously expected, or that the potential economic gains might be smaller than anticipated.

A slowdown in momentum could expose growing leverage in the AI sector, potentially exacerbating any shock through forced selling and increased volatility. For example, hyperscalers now account for 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance, up from less than 1% in 2024.
"The consequences of an AI correction could be global," the IMF warned, urging policymakers to curb excessive leverage, including through derivatives and margin loans.

The IMF said bond market risks had worsened since its April report, as higher energy prices pushed government bond yields upwards. Policymakers may need to raise interest rates to tackle inflation, potentially worsening debt burdens for countries refinancing short-term debt. In addition, more price-sensitive investors could put further upward pressure on yields, while market liquidity could deteriorate amid increased volatility.

Each of these factors could trigger a sudden rise in bond yields, the IMF warned, adding that historically high sovereign debt levels and unresolved fiscal deficits in major economies were intensifying the pressure.

However, bond markets had so far weathered the stress, with hedge funds able to unwind some of their borrowing through repurchase agreements without triggering turmoil in repo markets, it said. The IMF urged policymakers to put public debt on a sustainable path.

The fund also warned that technological developments and growing reliance on a small number of critical service providers were making cyber defence more difficult. In more than 70% of cases so far in 2026, software providers had almost no time to patch vulnerabilities before they were exploited, a rise of 20 percentage points from a year earlier, the IMF said.
AI could help address some of these risks, but AI models were also making cyberattacks more sophisticated.

A major attack affecting a critical service or financial institution could undermine confidence and quickly send shockwaves through financial markets, the IMF cautioned. It urged policymakers to strengthen cybersecurity capabilities, including through stricter oversight of third-party technology vendors.

The IMF said its stress-test models showed that banks' capital buffers remained robust even under a hypothetical downturn triggered by an AI slowdown and bond market fragility. However, it warned of "pockets of weakness", with banks accounting for 22% of global banking assets found to have weak capital levels under the test, up from 18% in the 2025 assessment.

extraction.body: LOS ANGELES , Oct. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR ), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company that has proposed to acquire Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc.'s (NASDAQ: FFAI ) EAI Robotics business, today highlighted FFAI's announcement that this week's Investor Weekly Report from Faraday Future ("FF") Founder and Global CEO YT Jia has been rescheduled to October 14. Additionally, FFR and FFAI will host a joint new product launch event on October 14, 2026, featuring four major launches focused on embodied AI robotics, Physical AI education, and developer enablement. The event will feature FF Nova, FF's first embodied AI humanoid robot designed for developers and educational institutions, through an exclusive, invitation-only launch. FFAI has also announced that FF will introduce FF Nova Mini, a humanoid robot designed for foundational Physical AI education, along with the EAI Education Ecosystem Brain and Curriculum Skills 2.0. In addition, FF will launch the FF Nova Developer Reinforcement Learning Platform and open exclusive early access to the developer community. FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR ) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI (EAI) robotics company that is in the process of acquiring the FF EAI Robotics business. Upon completion of the acquisition, the Company will focus on the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization, and deployment of intelligent robotic technologies, products, and industry solutions. The Company is committed to building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of EAI Brain & Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions, and EAI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," the Company aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified EAI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications. The FF EAI Robotics business has already achieved commercial deliveries of humanoid and biomimetic robotic products. Through its multi-form-factor robotic products, EAI technology platform, closed-loop data capabilities, and industry solutions, the business continues to advance the scaled adoption of robotics across real-world applications. The Company also operates RoboShare, a robot-sharing and services platform designed to connect robotic assets, service capabilities, customer demand, and ecosystem partners, further strengthening its robotics commercialization and service ecosystem. Faraday Future Announces This Week’s Investor Weekly Report from YT Jia Has Been Rescheduled to October 14; FFR and FFAI to Host Joint New Product Launch Event on October 14 Faraday Future Announces This Week’s Investor Weekly Report from YT Jia Has Been Rescheduled to October 14; FFR and FFAI to Host Joint New Product Launch Event on October 14 SOFIA, Bulgaria (AP) — Drones struck two ships in the Black Sea off Bulgaria on Tuesday, sinking one and prompting emergency rescue operations, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members from one ship, the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries, Radev said in a video posted to social media. The crew, which included seven Ukrainian citizens and eight Azerbaijan citizens, reported the ship's deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones. One crew member from the sunken vessel was rescued, Radev added, without providing details about the others aboard. The strikes on the two ships occurred 18 and 17 miles (29 and 27.5 kilometers) from the Bulgarian coast. During an emergency meeting of Bulgaria’s Security Council on Tuesday, Radev called the attacks “absolutely unacceptable” and said Bulgaria was seeking NATO and European Union assistance. While authorities do not possess clear evidence on who was responsible for the drone attacks, “logic, as I have already stated, indicates that the result is in favor of the Russian Federation,” Radev said. The attacks come exactly a week after sea and aerial drones attacked two other commercial vessels in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea. A Togo-flagged ship sank, while a Bulgarian ferry evacuated the 18-member crew from a Pulau-flagged vessel. Ukraine’s military did not conduct any operations near the locations of last week's drone strikes, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who pointed the finger at Russia. A day earlier, a Turkish-owned cargo ship carrying corn caught fire following a drone attack and later sank in the Black Sea off the coast of Romania. Two people died and 11 crew members were rescued, Romanian authorities said. Russia did not immediately comment on Tuesday's incident. Radev said he would summon the Russian ambassador to Bulgaria, Eleonora Mitrofanova, for a conversation Tuesday. Additionally, FFR and FFAI will host a joint new product launch event on October 14, 2026, featuring four major launches focused on embodied AI robotics, Physical AI education, and developer enablement. The event will feature FF Nova, FF's first embodied AI humanoid robot designed for developers and educational institutions, through an exclusive, invitation-only launch. FFAI has also announced that FF will introduce FF Nova Mini, a humanoid robot designed for foundational Physical AI education, along with the EAI Education Ecosystem Brain and Curriculum Skills 2.0. In addition, FF will launch the FF Nova Developer Reinforcement Learning Platform and open exclusive early access to the developer community. FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR ) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI (EAI) robotics company that is in the process of acquiring the FF EAI Robotics business. The Company is committed to building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of EAI Brain & Developer Platform, EAI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions, and EAI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," the Company aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified EAI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications. The FF EAI Robotics business has already achieved commercial deliveries of humanoid and biomimetic robotic products. Through its multi-form-factor robotic products, EAI technology platform, closed-loop data capabilities, and industry solutions, the business continues to advance the scaled adoption of robotics across real-world applications. Faraday Future Announces This Week’s Investor Weekly Report from YT Jia Has Been Rescheduled to October 14; FFR and FFAI to Host Joint New Product Launch Event on October 14 Faraday Future Announces This Week’s Investor Weekly Report from YT Jia Has Been Rescheduled to October 14; FFR and FFAI to Host Joint New Product Launch Event on October 14 SOFIA, Bulgaria (AP) — Drones struck two ships in the Black Sea off Bulgaria on Tuesday, sinking one and prompting emergency rescue operations, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members from one ship, the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries, Radev said in a video posted to social media. The crew, which included seven Ukrainian citizens and eight Azerbaijan citizens, reported the ship's deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones. One crew member from the sunken vessel was rescued, Radev added, without providing details about the others aboard. The strikes on the two ships occurred 18 and 17 miles (29 and 27.5 kilometers) from the Bulgarian coast. During an emergency meeting of Bulgaria’s Security Council on Tuesday, Radev called the attacks “absolutely unacceptable” and said Bulgaria was seeking NATO and European Union assistance. While authorities do not possess clear evidence on who was responsible for the drone attacks, “logic, as I have already stated, indicates that the result is in favor of the Russian Federation,” Radev said. The attacks come exactly a week after sea and aerial drones attacked two other commercial vessels in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea. A Togo-flagged ship sank, while a Bulgarian ferry evacuated the 18-member crew from a Pulau-flagged vessel. Ukraine’s military did not conduct any operations near the locations of last week's drone strikes, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who pointed the finger at Russia. A day earlier, a Turkish-owned cargo ship carrying corn caught fire following a drone attack and later sank in the Black Sea off the coast of Romania. Two people died and 11 crew members were rescued, Romanian authorities said. Russia did not immediately comment on Tuesday's incident. Radev said he would summon the Russian ambassador to Bulgaria, Eleonora Mitrofanova, for a conversation Tuesday. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev speaks during a handover ceremony of the remains of medieval ruler Czar Samuel, in Thessaloniki, northern Greece, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. The proposed transaction includes up to $150 million in performance-based earn-outs linked to specified business milestones. The number of IonQ common shares to be issued will be calculated using a volume-weighted average price, subject to a collar ranging from $33.07 to $49.61 per share . The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to required regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The agreement remains pending until the transaction is completed. Founded in 2019, Elisity develops an identity-based microsegmentation platform that helps organizations manage network access across information technology (IT), operational technology (OT), Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and enterprise workloads. According to the companies’ transaction announcement, Elisity has more than 100 customer deployments worldwide, providing IonQ with an established enterprise cybersecurity presence. The acquisition comes as organizations assess the long-term implications of quantum computing for existing encryption systems. One major concern is the harvest now, decrypt later (HNDL) threat, in which attackers collect and store encrypted information today in the hope of decrypting it in the future using more powerful computing capabilities. Widely deployed public-key cryptographic systems, including those based on RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography (ECC), could be vulnerable to sufficiently capable quantum computers. However, the timeline for developing machines capable of breaking these systems at scale remains uncertain. IonQ intends to combine its quantum security technologies with Elisity’s zero-trust capabilities to address complementary aspects of enterprise cybersecurity. Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is designed to protect information against attacks from future quantum computers, while identity-based microsegmentation restricts unauthorized communications within enterprise networks. Microsegmentation can reduce the ability of attackers to move laterally after compromising an initial device or system. It does not, however, independently prevent the future decryption of encrypted data that has already been intercepted. Organizations facing HNDL risks must also assess their cryptographic systems, protect sensitive information, and plan migrations to appropriate post-quantum standards. IonQ Chief Executive Officer Niccolo de Masi has positioned the transaction as part of the company’s broader effort to expand its security offerings and help customers prepare for the quantum era. The acquisition could provide IonQ with additional enterprise relationships through which to introduce complementary cybersecurity and cryptographic products. IonQ’s earlier acquisition of SkyWater Technology expanded its capabilities in semiconductor manufacturing and related technologies. Elisity would add an established enterprise security platform, creating opportunities to connect quantum security offerings with network access controls used by corporate and government customers. Cryptographic protection: IonQ’s quantum networking and security initiatives include technologies intended to support secure communications and the transition toward quantum-resistant protection. Enterprise network enforcement: Elisity’s identity-based microsegmentation platform helps security teams apply least-privilege access policies to users, devices, applications, workloads, and other network entities. The companies expect the combination to create opportunities for cross-selling, strengthen relationships with enterprise security teams, and support the development of integrated security products. extraction.body: IonQ has agreed to buy cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, expanding its security business as advances in quantum computing and artificial intelligence raise concerns about cyberattacks. The transaction includes up to $150 million in additional payments tied to Elisity’s future performance, executives told The Wall Street Journal . IonQ Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi told the newspaper that the acquisition reflects his expectation that companies will need stronger defenses as both technologies become more powerful. “With Elisity and its team as part of IonQ , we will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era. As I said first, Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted. IonQ is offering its customers a vertically integrated full-stack quantum platform across quantum computing, networking, sensing and cybersecurity. Just as adding SkyWater Technology expanded IonQ’s capabilities in chip design, fabrication and packaging, Elisity will bring proven enterprise policy enforcement scale and deployment experience to our quantum security strategy and will give IonQ a strong growth platform to serve customers and create value for our shareholders,” Niccolo de Masi, Chairman and CEO of IonQ, said in a statement . Elisity, founded in 2019, provides software designed to stop attackers and ransomware from spreading through an organization’s network. Its major customers include health care companies and hospitals, according to the WSJ. “Our customers need to prioritize post-quantum cryptography initiatives while securing existing assets to keep essential operations running,” James Winebrenner, CEO of Elisity, said in the release. “With IonQ, we will be optimally positioned to partner with them to modernize their crypto-agility programs, accelerate post-quantum cryptography capabilities while advancing their holistic Zero Trust posture and deploy hybrid-cybersecurity solutions today that are prepared for the quantum future.” The purchase would bring that business into IonQ , which develops quantum computers and has been buying companies to offer customers a broader range of technology. Winebrenner is expected to remain after the transaction closes, the WSJ reported. De Masi told the Journal that the combined companies would seek to help customers address growing security risks, including threats involving AI agents. These are software systems that can carry out tasks with some degree of independence, rather than simply respond to individual questions. The acquisition brings together businesses addressing different parts of the computing and security market. IonQ is developing machines intended to tackle certain problems beyond the practical reach of conventional computers. Elisity focuses on limiting the damage attackers can cause after entering an organization’s network. Preventing an intrusion from spreading is a central part of that defense. An attacker who gains access to one system may try to reach other computers and sensitive information. Ransomware can compound the damage by locking organizations out of their files or systems. Elisity’s platform aims to contain that movement, according to the WSJ. The proposed acquisition would give IonQ an established cybersecurity offering and customers with immediate security needs. The WSJ also reported growing concern among businesses and government officials about unauthorized activity involving AI systems. De Masi presented those risks as part of the rationale for combining the companies. De Masi told the WSJ that American companies and the federal government must prepare for “Q-Day,” the point at which quantum computers become powerful enough to defeat widely used public-key cryptography. “The bad guys are going to keep taking advantage of new technology,” De Masi told the WSJ. “Unfortunately, we are entering the most dangerous years, vis-à-vis cybersecurity risks.” Public-key cryptography helps protect information and verify identities online. The concern is that sufficiently capable quantum computers could undermine some of the mathematical methods supporting those protections. That potential threat differs from the spread of an attacker through a network, which Elisity’s software is designed to address. De Masi’s comments place the acquisition within a broader effort to help customers manage security risks associated with increasingly capable computing systems. IonQ specializes in trapped-ion quantum computers, which use electrically charged atoms to store and process quantum information. The company is pursuing applications ranging from drug discovery to national defense. The newspaper reported that the Trump administration’s support for quantum technology has helped the business. Over the summer, President Donald Trump signed executive orders promoting the development of a powerful quantum computer and protection of government systems against related cyber threats. The Elisity agreement follows IonQ ’s $1.8 billion deal earlier this year to acquire chipmaker SkyWater Technology, likely its largest acquisition to date. IonQ , which works closely with the Defense Department, has pursued acquisitions to become a broader technology supplier for its customers, the newspaper reported. Under the Elisity agreement, the number of IonQ shares issued will be calculated using a share price between $33.07 and $49.61, executives told the WSJ. IonQ shares closed Friday at $39.89, giving the company a market value of nearly $16 billion. Currently, the company is trading down 2% in pre-market trading. The company empowers satellite-based quantum networks and quantum enabled drones to improve positioning, navigation, and timing resilience in GPS denied environments, and collaborates with industry leaders like Airbus to optimize aircraft loading. Elisity has a strong track record of doubling its revenue and its customer base year-over-year with zero churn among deployed customers.

With more than 100 global customer deployments and deep CISO and security community relationships, Elisity will provide IonQ with expanded channels to bring its PQC, QKD and quantum computing offerings to market for both enterprise and government networks, opening up the more than $10 billion microsegmentation opportunity with double-digit CAGR to IonQ.

The number of IonQ shares to be issued in the transaction will be calculated at closing based on the volume-weighted average price of IonQ common stock for the 20 trading days prior to, but not including, the third business day before the closing date, but that price will not be greater than $49.61 or less than $33.07 per share.

extraction.body: IonQ, a full-stack quantum platform and foundry company, announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Elisity Inc. , a Zero Trust security company, in an all-stock transaction valued at up to $1.3 billion. The acquisition brings together IonQ’s post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and quantum key distribution (QKD) capabilities with Elisity’s enterprise Zero Trust technology platform. On a combined basis, IonQ will benefit from an expanded cybersecurity platform that both uncovers and protects against present LLM and emerging quantum threats. Elisity builds on IonQ’s expanding quantum security offerings with a high-growth enterprise security business, cutting-edge Zero Trust technology platform, and team of industry leaders led by cybersecurity expert CEO James Winebrenner. Elisity has a strong track record of doubling its revenue and its customer base year-over-year with zero churn among deployed customers. With more than 100 global customer deployments and deep CISO and security community relationships, Elisity will provide IonQ with expanded channels to bring its PQC, QKD and quantum computing offerings to market for both enterprise and government networks, opening up the more than $10 billion microsegmentation opportunity with double-digit CAGR to IonQ. “With Elisity and its team as part of IonQ, we will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era,” said Niccolo de Masi, chairman and CEO of IonQ. “As I said first, Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted. IonQ is offering its customers a vertically integrated full-stack quantum platform across quantum computing, networking, sensing and cybersecurity. Just as adding SkyWater Technology expanded IonQ’s capabilities in chip design, fabrication and packaging, Elisity will bring proven enterprise policy enforcement scale and deployment experience to our quantum security strategy and will give IonQ a strong growth platform to serve customers and create value for our shareholders.” “Our customers need to prioritize post-quantum cryptography initiatives while securing existing assets to keep essential operations running,” said James Winebrenner, CEO of Elisity. “With IonQ, we will be optimally positioned to partner with them to modernize their crypto-agility programs, accelerate post-quantum cryptography capabilities while advancing their holistic Zero Trust posture and deploy hybrid-cybersecurity solutions today that are prepared for the quantum future.” Enterprises face two overlapping priorities: containing attacks that operate at machine speed and preparing to protect sensitive information against future quantum threats. The urgency of this transition is underscored by recent White House executive orders advancing quantum innovation and accelerating the federal government’s migration to PQC. These directives reinforce the importance of securing critical systems and preparing government networks for quantum-era threats while supporting long-term modernization. Elisity IdentityGraph combines native asset identity and partner-enriched context, and risk information to inform least-privilege access policy for users, devices, workloads and AI agents. Teams can simulate policies before limiting each identity to the communications it needs, helping reduce attack surface and contain an attack’s spread. By bringing together Elisity’s Zero Trust framework with IonQ’s PQC and QKD capabilities, the companies will combine cryptographic protection for sensitive information and communications with identity-based controls that limit unauthorized access and the spread of threats across enterprise networks. The shared roadmap with IonQ will extend IdentityGraph with cryptographic inventory and risk information. This integrated approach will help customers address quantum-related security risks through a multiyear transition while strengthening defenses against current cyberattacks, including threats involving AI agents. Following closing, Elisity will continue serving its customers under its current leadership, including current CEO James Winebrenner. Together, the companies will continue their track record of innovation, customer success and strong partner relationships, backed by IonQ’s demonstrated approach of investing in the critical technologies it acquires. IonQ brings an established track record in growing its quantum security and quantum-secure communications offering. The company has deployed some of the largest quantum-safe national communications networks in the world, including in Switzerland, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia, and serves global customers with quantum-safe defense in depth spanning quantum-safe posture management, quantum key distribution, and post-quantum cryptography. Customers are increasingly adopting multiple IonQ products and services, driving growth in multiproduct revenue and providing evidence of demand for integrated solutions; in the second quarter of 2026, IonQ delivered 40% year-over-year growth in multiproduct revenue. IonQ and Elisity expect opportunities to cross-sell complementary security solutions, expand relationships with enterprise and government customers, and develop integrated offerings. Under the terms of the agreement, IonQ will acquire Elisity in an all-stock transaction valued at up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in earnout opportunity subject to performance of the Elisity business. The number of IonQ shares to be issued in the transaction will be calculated at closing based on the volume-weighted average price of IonQ common stock for the 20 trading days prior to, but not including, the third business day before the closing date, but that price will not be greater than $49.61 or less than $33.07 per share. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is subject to customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approval.

extraction.body: IonQ will acquire Zero Trust security firm Elisity in an all-stock transaction valued at up to $1.3 billion, pairing IonQ’s quantum cryptography with Elisity’s enterprise security platform. The acquisition aims to address current cyber threats and prepare customers for the approaching quantum era, a transition highlighted by recent White House directives. Elisity has demonstrated significant growth, “doubling its revenue and its customer base year-over-year,” and brings a strong foothold in the more than $10 billion microsegmentation market. “With Elisity and its team as part of IonQ, we will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure,” said Niccolo de Masi , Chairman and CEO of IonQ. IonQ’s acquisition of Elisity directly addresses the escalating need for layered cybersecurity, integrating Zero Trust principles with emerging quantum defenses. This move aligns with a recent White House executive order from June 22, 2026, which prioritizes quantum innovation and the federal government’s transition to PQC standards. Elisity’s core offering, IdentityGraph, correlates identity, asset and risk information to enforce least-privilege access policies for users, devices and increasingly, AI agents. Teams can simulate these policies before implementation, reducing attack surfaces and limiting the spread of potential breaches. By integrating IdentityGraph with IonQ’s cryptographic protections, the companies aim to offer a solution that not only safeguards sensitive data with PQC and QKD but also controls who and what can access it, creating a multi-layered defense. The combined roadmap will extend IdentityGraph with cryptographic inventory and risk information, enhancing its capabilities for quantum-era security. The urgency of this integration is highlighted by the dual challenges enterprises currently face: containing attacks operating at machine speed and preparing for the long-term threat posed by quantum computers. “Our customers need to prioritize cryptography initiatives while securing existing assets to keep essential operations running,” said James Winebrenner, CEO of Elisity. “With IonQ, we will be optimally positioned to partner with them to modernize their crypto-agility programs, accelerate cryptography capabilities while advancing their holistic Zero Trust posture and deploy hybrid-cybersecurity solutions today that are prepared for the quantum future.” Elisity’s existing customer base, exceeding 100 global deployments and including deep relationships with Chief Information Security Officers, provides IonQ with an expanded channel to market its quantum security offerings to both enterprise and government networks. IonQ anticipates significant cross-selling opportunities, using Elisity’s established enterprise presence to introduce its PQC, QKD and broader quantum computing services. This acquisition builds upon IonQ’s existing momentum in quantum security, having already deployed quantum-safe national communications networks in Switzerland, Poland, Romania and Slovakia, and serving global customers with quantum-safe defense-in-depth solutions. In the second quarter of 2026, IonQ reported 40 percent year-over-year growth in multiproduct revenue, demonstrating customer demand for integrated quantum solutions. The strategic rationale behind the acquisition extends beyond immediate security enhancements. As de Masi first stated, the arrival of Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted. He drew a parallel to the acquisition of SkyWater Technology , noting that Elisity will bring proven enterprise policy enforcement scale and deployment experience to IonQ’s quantum security strategy, establishing a strong growth platform for serving customers and creating shareholder value. Elisity will continue operating under its current leadership, including CEO James Winebrenner, ensuring continuity for existing customers and partners. The company, founded in 2019, has a global employee footprint and a growing number of Fortune 500 clients, IonQ says. IonQ’s approach of investing in acquired technologies suggests a commitment to supporting innovation and building upon Elisity’s existing strengths, creating a synergistic relationship that addresses the evolving landscape of cybersecurity threats. The transaction, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approval. As I said first, Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted. One major concern is the harvest now, decrypt later (HNDL) threat, in which attackers collect and store encrypted information today in the hope of decrypting it in the future using more powerful computing capabilities. Widely deployed public-key cryptographic systems, including those based on RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography (ECC), could be vulnerable to sufficiently capable quantum computers. Organizations facing HNDL risks must also assess their cryptographic systems, protect sensitive information, and plan migrations to appropriate post-quantum standards. Elisity’s platform aims to contain that movement, according to the WSJ. The proposed acquisition would give IonQ an established cybersecurity offering and customers with immediate security needs.

The WSJ also reported growing concern among businesses and government officials about unauthorized activity involving AI systems. De Masi presented those risks as part of the rationale for combining the companies.

De Masi told the WSJ that American companies and the federal government must prepare for “Q-Day,” the point at which quantum computers become powerful enough to defeat widely used public-key cryptography.
“The bad guys are going to keep taking advantage of new technology,” De Masi told the WSJ. “Unfortunately, we are entering the most dangerous years, vis-à-vis cybersecurity risks.”

Public-key cryptography helps protect information and verify identities online. The concern is that sufficiently capable quantum computers could undermine some of the mathematical methods supporting those protections.

That potential threat differs from the spread of an attacker through a network, which Elisity’s software is designed to address. De Masi’s comments place the acquisition within a broader effort to help customers manage security risks associated with increasingly capable computing systems.

IonQ specializes in trapped-ion quantum computers, which use electrically charged atoms to store and process quantum information. The company is pursuing applications ranging from drug discovery to national defense.

The newspaper reported that the Trump administration’s support for quantum technology has helped the business. Over the summer, President Donald Trump signed executive orders promoting the development of a powerful quantum computer and protection of government systems against related cyber threats.
The Elisity agreement follows IonQ ’s $1.8 billion deal earlier this year to acquire chipmaker SkyWater Technology, likely its largest acquisition to date.
IonQ , which works closely with the Defense Department, has pursued acquisitions to become a broader technology supplier for its customers, the newspaper reported.

Under the Elisity agreement, the number of IonQ shares issued will be calculated using a share price between $33.07 and $49.61, executives told the WSJ. IonQ shares closed Friday at $39.89, giving the company a market value of nearly $16 billion. Currently, the company is trading down 2% in pre-market trading.

The company empowers satellite-based quantum networks and quantum enabled drones to improve positioning, navigation, and timing resilience in GPS denied environments, and collaborates with industry leaders like Airbus to optimize aircraft loading.

extraction.body: IonQ, a full-stack quantum platform and foundry company, announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Elisity Inc. , a Zero Trust security company, in an all-stock transaction valued at up to $1.3 billion. The acquisition brings together IonQ’s post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and quantum key distribution (QKD) capabilities with Elisity’s enterprise Zero Trust technology platform. On a combined basis, IonQ will benefit from an expanded cybersecurity platform that both uncovers and protects against present LLM and emerging quantum threats. Elisity builds on IonQ’s expanding quantum security offerings with a high-growth enterprise security business, cutting-edge Zero Trust technology platform, and team of industry leaders led by cybersecurity expert CEO James Winebrenner. Elisity has a strong track record of doubling its revenue and its customer base year-over-year with zero churn among deployed customers. With more than 100 global customer deployments and deep CISO and security community relationships, Elisity will provide IonQ with expanded channels to bring its PQC, QKD and quantum computing offerings to market for both enterprise and government networks, opening up the more than $10 billion microsegmentation opportunity with double-digit CAGR to IonQ. “With Elisity and its team as part of IonQ, we will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era,” said Niccolo de Masi, chairman and CEO of IonQ. “As I said first, Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted. IonQ is offering its customers a vertically integrated full-stack quantum platform across quantum computing, networking, sensing and cybersecurity. Just as adding SkyWater Technology expanded IonQ’s capabilities in chip design, fabrication and packaging, Elisity will bring proven enterprise policy enforcement scale and deployment experience to our quantum security strategy and will give IonQ a strong growth platform to serve customers and create value for our shareholders.” “Our customers need to prioritize post-quantum cryptography initiatives while securing existing assets to keep essential operations running,” said James Winebrenner, CEO of Elisity. “With IonQ, we will be optimally positioned to partner with them to modernize their crypto-agility programs, accelerate post-quantum cryptography capabilities while advancing their holistic Zero Trust posture and deploy hybrid-cybersecurity solutions today that are prepared for the quantum future.” Enterprises face two overlapping priorities: containing attacks that operate at machine speed and preparing to protect sensitive information against future quantum threats. The urgency of this transition is underscored by recent White House executive orders advancing quantum innovation and accelerating the federal government’s migration to PQC. These directives reinforce the importance of securing critical systems and preparing government networks for quantum-era threats while supporting long-term modernization. Elisity IdentityGraph combines native asset identity and partner-enriched context, and risk information to inform least-privilege access policy for users, devices, workloads and AI agents. Teams can simulate policies before limiting each identity to the communications it needs, helping reduce attack surface and contain an attack’s spread. By bringing together Elisity’s Zero Trust framework with IonQ’s PQC and QKD capabilities, the companies will combine cryptographic protection for sensitive information and communications with identity-based controls that limit unauthorized access and the spread of threats across enterprise networks. The shared roadmap with IonQ will extend IdentityGraph with cryptographic inventory and risk information. This integrated approach will help customers address quantum-related security risks through a multiyear transition while strengthening defenses against current cyberattacks, including threats involving AI agents. Following closing, Elisity will continue serving its customers under its current leadership, including current CEO James Winebrenner. Together, the companies will continue their track record of innovation, customer success and strong partner relationships, backed by IonQ’s demonstrated approach of investing in the critical technologies it acquires. IonQ brings an established track record in growing its quantum security and quantum-secure communications offering. The company has deployed some of the largest quantum-safe national communications networks in the world, including in Switzerland, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia, and serves global customers with quantum-safe defense in depth spanning quantum-safe posture management, quantum key distribution, and post-quantum cryptography. Customers are increasingly adopting multiple IonQ products and services, driving growth in multiproduct revenue and providing evidence of demand for integrated solutions; in the second quarter of 2026, IonQ delivered 40% year-over-year growth in multiproduct revenue. IonQ and Elisity expect opportunities to cross-sell complementary security solutions, expand relationships with enterprise and government customers, and develop integrated offerings. Under the terms of the agreement, IonQ will acquire Elisity in an all-stock transaction valued at up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in earnout opportunity subject to performance of the Elisity business. The number of IonQ shares to be issued in the transaction will be calculated at closing based on the volume-weighted average price of IonQ common stock for the 20 trading days prior to, but not including, the third business day before the closing date, but that price will not be greater than $49.61 or less than $33.07 per share. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is subject to customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approval.

sources.title: Vietnam's edtech market surges with AI-driven, locally adapted platforms - Báo VietNamNet
passages: Amid this shift, Coursera, a global online learning platform, has emerged as a leader in adapting to Vietnam’s rapidly changing tech landscape.

Greg Hart, CEO of Coursera, noted that the platform currently has about 1.8 million learners in Vietnam, ranking third in Southeast Asia behind the Philippines (2.8 million) and Indonesia (2.1 million).
Vietnamese users are particularly drawn to data science, AI, and Chinese language courses.
Despite its vast potential, Vietnam’s edtech market faces hurdles such as affordability, users’ preference for free or partially paid models, and the challenge of retaining learners long-term.

However, national digital transformation policies, AI development commitments, and efforts to popularize digital skills in education are creating tangible growth opportunities for market participants.
Many have integrated livestream classes, support teachers, 24/7 learning chatbots, and exam prep content aligned with Vietnam’s national education curriculum.
These domestic players have a deep understanding of local student and parent psychology – a decisive advantage in a cost-sensitive and trust-driven market.
Vietnam’s online education sector is shifting from a “tech pilot” phase to a “content and experience strategy” phase.
This surge is fueled not only by the digital transformation of education but also by remote work trends and the need for lifelong learning in the face of rapidly evolving labor market demands.
Local edtech start-ups like Vuihoc.vn, Edupia, Moon.vn, and Topica are also accelerating, investing in AI and adaptive learning models that personalize learning progress for individual students.
The widespread impact of artificial intelligence (AI), especially generative models like ChatGPT, has dramatically transformed industries, and education is among the first to feel the change.

extraction.body: The localization race: From language to experience The widespread impact of artificial intelligence (AI), especially generative models like ChatGPT, has dramatically transformed industries, and education is among the first to feel the change. While grappling with challenges around effectiveness, the sector is also seeing unprecedented opportunities for expansion. Global edtech is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13.6%, reaching $348 billion by 2030. This surge is fueled not only by the digital transformation of education but also by remote work trends and the need for lifelong learning in the face of rapidly evolving labor market demands. According to a World Economic Forum (WEF) report, 44% of today’s workforce skills will become obsolete within five years. The rise of AI makes competencies like data science, coding, and big data essential. Meanwhile, irreplaceable human skills such as critical thinking, creativity, problem-solving, and analysis are becoming top priorities for corporate training programs. Victory will only go to those who truly “speak Vietnamese” – both literally and figuratively. Amid this shift, Coursera, a global online learning platform, has emerged as a leader in adapting to Vietnam’s rapidly changing tech landscape. Greg Hart, CEO of Coursera, noted that the platform currently has about 1.8 million learners in Vietnam, ranking third in Southeast Asia behind the Philippines (2.8 million) and Indonesia (2.1 million). Vietnamese users are particularly drawn to data science, AI, and Chinese language courses. Local edtech start-ups like Vuihoc.vn, Edupia, Moon.vn, and Topica are also accelerating, investing in AI and adaptive learning models that personalize learning progress for individual students. Many have integrated livestream classes, support teachers, 24/7 learning chatbots, and exam prep content aligned with Vietnam’s national education curriculum. These domestic players have a deep understanding of local student and parent psychology – a decisive advantage in a cost-sensitive and trust-driven market. Despite its vast potential, Vietnam’s edtech market faces hurdles such as affordability, users’ preference for free or partially paid models, and the challenge of retaining learners long-term. However, national digital transformation policies, AI development commitments, and efforts to popularize digital skills in education are creating tangible growth opportunities for market participants. The race for experience and content, not just tech Vietnam’s online education sector is shifting from a “tech pilot” phase to a “content and experience strategy” phase. Localization now means more than translating content - it involves a deep understanding of Vietnamese learners: their learning styles, parental expectations, classroom culture, curricula, and spending capacity. The battle between international platforms and local start-ups is playing out across multiple dimensions: technology, culture, and trust. While technology offers an advantage, it is no longer a barrier. Victory will go to those who truly “speak Vietnamese,” in every sense. Though promising, online learning still faces the paradox of high accessibility but low effectiveness. Studies show that completion rates for massive open online courses (MOOCs) remain low. However, the integration of AI is beginning to change that. Tools like Coach offer instant feedback, allow learners to ask questions, practice, and track personalized progress - features previously available only in low student-teacher ratio classrooms. The combination of human and AI interaction is creating a more effective, immersive learning experience. Edtech’s story cannot be separated from global employment trends. According to WEF’s 2023 report, around 83 million jobs will disappear over the next five years, while only 69 million new ones will be created - resulting in a net loss of 14 million. Repetitive, low-skill roles are likely to be the first replaced by technology. Conversely, new roles are emerging rapidly, requiring a flexible workforce committed to lifelong learning and adaptation. Interdisciplinary skills such as digital-era critical thinking, cross-cultural literacy, and fluency in AI tools are becoming essential survival credentials.

This surge is largely attributed to widespread adoption of digital education tools, improved internet access facilitating online learning, heightened demand for customized educational experiences, the expansion of e-learning offerings in academic institutions, and growing investments in education technology solutions.

LONDON, GREATER LONDON, UNITED KINGDOM, October 12, 2026 / EINPresswire.com / -- The landscape of education technology is rapidly evolving, with artificial intelligence (AI) playing a pivotal role in transforming personalized learning experiences.
This overview delves into the current market status, growth drivers, regional dynamics, and key trends shaping this innovative sector.
These systems dynamically adjust instructional materials, learning speed, and assessments to suit individual needs while offering intelligent guidance and feedback.
By leveraging data-driven insights and automated support, these platforms enhance educational outcomes through continuous optimization of the learning process.
Personalized learning involves crafting educational paths, content, and assessments tailored to each learner’s unique preferences, abilities, and progress.
This demand has surged alongside the rapid integration of digital learning technologies that support adaptive, student-centered education models.

AI-powered platforms harness machine learning algorithms to provide customized lessons, intelligent tutoring, performance monitoring, and immediate feedback, catering to individual learner requirements.

The market analysis encompasses various geographical areas including Asia-Pacific, South East Asia, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, North America, South America, the Middle East, and Africa, offering a detailed global perspective on market trends and expansion opportunities.

Key trends anticipated during the forecast period involve the adoption of personalized learning path generation, real-time learner performance analytics, adaptive assessment technologies, intelligent student engagement and feedback mechanisms, as well as platforms designed to automate learning outcome optimization.
Such evidence highlights the growing appreciation and demand for personalized education solutions, which in turn fuels market growth.

Market Size and Projected Expansion of the AI-Powered Personalized Learning and EdTech Tutoring Platforms Market The market for AI-driven personalized learning and EdTech tutoring platforms has experienced remarkable expansion recently. It is projected to grow from $8.08 billion in 2025 to $10.03 billion in 2026, reflecting a strong compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.0%. This surge is largely attributed to widespread adoption of digital education tools, improved internet access facilitating online learning, heightened demand for customized educational experiences, the expansion of e-learning offerings in academic institutions, and growing investments in education technology solutions. Forecasted Growth and Future Potential of the AI-Powered Personalized Learning and EdTech Tutoring Platforms Market Looking ahead, this market is expected to witness exponential growth, reaching $23.42 billion by 2030 with a CAGR of 23.6%. Drivers behind this robust growth include increasing demand for AI-enabled personalized learning, wider adoption of intelligent tutoring systems, greater investments directed toward adaptive educational technologies, enhanced utilization of learning analytics platforms, and a stronger focus on lifelong digital learning. Key trends anticipated during the forecast period involve the adoption of personalized learning path generation, real-time learner performance analytics, adaptive assessment technologies, intelligent student engagement and feedback mechanisms, as well as platforms designed to automate learning outcome optimization. Understanding AI-Powered Personalized Learning and EdTech Tutoring Platforms AI-powered personalized learning and EdTech tutoring platforms employ artificial intelligence to continuously monitor learner performance, preferences, and progress in real time. These systems dynamically adjust instructional materials, learning speed, and assessments to suit individual needs while offering intelligent guidance and feedback. By leveraging data-driven insights and automated support, these platforms enhance educational outcomes through continuous optimization of the learning process. Increasing Demand for Customized Learning Experiences Driving Market Growth The rising need for personalized learning experiences is a significant factor propelling the growth of AI-powered personalized learning and EdTech tutoring platforms. Personalized learning involves crafting educational paths, content, and assessments tailored to each learner’s unique preferences, abilities, and progress. This demand has surged alongside the rapid integration of digital learning technologies that support adaptive, student-centered education models. AI-powered platforms harness machine learning algorithms to provide customized lessons, intelligent tutoring, performance monitoring, and immediate feedback, catering to individual learner requirements. Demonstrated Effectiveness of AI in Enhancing Student Outcomes For example, in January 2025, the Science and Information Organization (SAI), a UK-based progressive institution, reported that AI-powered personalized learning significantly improved student performance. Learners using these platforms performed 25% better, completed tasks 25% faster, and exhibited 15% higher engagement compared to a control group. Such evidence highlights the growing appreciation and demand for personalized education solutions, which in turn fuels market growth. Regional Market Leaders and Growth Hotspots in AI-Powered Personalized Learning and EdTech Tutoring Platforms In 2025, North America held the largest share of the AI-powered personalized learning and EdTech tutoring platforms market. Key trends anticipated during the forecast period involve the adoption of personalized learning path generation, real-time learner performance analytics, adaptive assessment technologies, intelligent student engagement and feedback mechanisms, as well as platforms designed to automate learning outcome optimization.

Understanding AI-Powered Personalized Learning and EdTech Tutoring Platforms AI-powered personalized learning and EdTech tutoring platforms employ artificial intelligence to continuously monitor learner performance, preferences, and progress in real time. These systems dynamically adjust instructional materials, learning speed, and assessments to suit individual needs while offering intelligent guidance and feedback. By leveraging data-driven insights and automated support, these platforms enhance educational outcomes through continuous optimization of the learning process.

Increasing Demand for Customized Learning Experiences Driving Market Growth The rising need for personalized learning experiences is a significant factor propelling the growth of AI-powered personalized learning and EdTech tutoring platforms. Personalized learning involves crafting educational paths, content, and assessments tailored to each learner’s unique preferences, abilities, and progress. This demand has surged alongside the rapid integration of digital learning technologies that support adaptive, student-centered education models. AI-powered platforms harness machine learning algorithms to provide customized lessons, intelligent tutoring, performance monitoring, and immediate feedback, catering to individual learner requirements.

Demonstrated Effectiveness of AI in Enhancing Student Outcomes For example, in January 2025, the Science and Information Organization (SAI), a UK-based progressive institution, reported that AI-powered personalized learning significantly improved student performance. Learners using these platforms performed 25% better, completed tasks 25% faster, and exhibited 15% higher engagement compared to a control group. Such evidence highlights the growing appreciation and demand for personalized education solutions, which in turn fuels market growth.

Regional Market Leaders and Growth Hotspots in AI-Powered Personalized Learning and EdTech Tutoring Platforms In 2025, North America held the largest share of the AI-powered personalized learning and EdTech tutoring platforms market. Meanwhile, Asia-Pacific is projected to be the fastest-growing region during the forecast period.
